artworks.title: Calais and Zetes Deliver Phineus from the Harpies
artworks.description: Picart's engraving for the Temple of the Muses stages the Argonautic rescue of the blind seer Phineus: the winged Boreads Calais and Zetes drive off the Harpies who have been snatching his food. Ocypete — 'Swift-wing' — is one of the named sisters in that flock (with Aello and Celaeno), the storm-spirits Hesiod and Apollonius send against Phineus until the sons of Boreas chase them across the sea. The print is the standard early-modern image of the Harpy episode that defines Ocypete's myth.

artworks.title: Harpies and a Male Figure (Ivory Relief)
artworks.description: A small ivory relief of about 570 BC in the Archaeological Museum of Delphi shows bird-bodied Harpies confronting a male figure in a scene linked to the Argonaut cycle — the same narrative in which Ocypete and her sisters torment Phineus until the Boreads intervene. Archaic ivory carving here already fixes the Harpy as a winged female monster, the visual type Ocypete inherits as one of the swift daughters of Thaumas and Electra (or of Typhon and Echidna, in variant genealogies).

artworks.title: A Harpy
artworks.description: Melchior Lorck's 1582 woodcut isolates the Harpy as a Renaissance monster study: a woman's torso fused to a raptor's body and claws. The print belongs to the early-modern bestiary tradition that kept Ocypete's kind — the bird-maidens of the Phineus episode — alive as emblems of snatching hunger and storm, independent of any single sister's name.

artworks.title: Harpy
artworks.description: Dosso Dossi's oil in the Museo del Prado (58.4 × 167.8 cm) presents a lone Harpy in a horizontal landscape — the Ferrarese painter's eerie take on the classical bird-woman. Without naming Ocypete, Aello, or Celaeno, the canvas belongs to the same iconographic family as the Argonautic sisters: divine punishment delivered on the wing. It is one of the finest High-Renaissance paintings of the type.

popCulture.title: Ocypete
popCulture.description: Swift-wing among the Harpies — Ocypete outflies the Boreads until exhaustion lands her on an ocean isle.

popCulture.title: Harpy
